sentences.text: The type specimen of Caviramus consists of three fragments of the lower jaw containing multicuspate teeth.
This animal possessed between twelve and seventeen teeth in its lower jaw.
Holes in the front of the lower jaw, which is part of the type specimen consisting of three fragments containing multicuspate teeth, suggest Caviramus had a soft-tissue structure or keratin covering.
Caviramus had a wingspan of approximately 135 centimeters.
The genus Caviramus was named in 2006 by Nadia Fröbisch and Jörg Fröbisch.
Researchers suggest Caviramus may have been a terrestrial forager based on its long limbs.
Caviramus likely used a soaring mode of flight due to its gracile wings.
Caviramus may have been a piscivore and potentially an underwater hunter.
A 2020 study by Matthew G. Baron classified Caviramus within the family Caviramidae.
Caviramus lived during the Late Triassic in the Northern Calcareous Alps of Switzerland.
This creature existed between 211.18 and 201.4 million years ago.
It is debated whether Raeticodactylus filisurensis is a synonym of Caviramus, with differences potentially explained by sex or age.
